Arena Watch — level 10 bots, 2v2 and 3v3, on a pitch that keeps changing

The real shared/sim.js and shared/bot-ai.js from football-mock, bundled and run in this page — a fresh random seed and (optionally) a freshly generated layout every match. Switch between the two formats the game actually matchmakes: 2v2 on the main arena and 3v3 on its own wider layout. Every named play the bots run is announced in words, and the panel on the right keeps score of which skills from the catalogue have actually appeared.

      What this page is for

      The two research handoffs in summery/bots logic handoff/ measured sixteen skills in hand-built fixtures. This page runs the opposite test: whole matches, at the difficulty a real level-10 player meets, on layouts the bots were never tuned against — and counts what the bots actually reach for. Everything below was measured with bot-skill-census.mjs (7 arenas × 4 × 60 s, seeded) and shows up live in the panels above.

      • Range, not aim, is the leak. A full-charge kick rolls 647 px on a 2000 px pitch, but the release ladder still shoots at the mouth from anywhere inside 1150 px (bot-ai.js:1727). Measured: 5.8 of 7.5 shots at goal per match — 77% — are fired from beyond the distance the ball can travel. Turn on Kick range and watch the ring: shots taken with the goal outside it cannot arrive.
      • Cover is modelled on the wrong pitch. pointInBush() takes no state and reads the default arena's three rectangles, so on every other layout the bots' stealth model is fiction. That is what the red ball marker shows: a loose ball the bots believe is hidden, with nobody inside the 110 px reveal radius, is invisible to both teams. Worst single blind spell measured: 48 s on the classic layout, 21 s on the one that ships.
      • Most tricks work; a few are unreachable. The bank shot (goalBank) fired zero times in 28 matches, the full catapult combo 0.07 times a match, the cannon pass (a mate's bomb flinging the carrier, ball attached) 0.04, and a bomb used to clear a loose ball 0.2. Bots also cannot fire a quick tap at all — aimed: fire at bot-ai.js:3124 makes every bot bullet an aimed shot — so slow stacks and the ⅓ super are player-only.
      • Passing is technically sound and tactically catchable. 80% of releases leave below FULL_CHARGE (0.70), and a kick under that threshold is caught outright by any field defender in the lane. The pass charge is sized by dist / 950, which only reaches full power at 665 px — past the 558 px where the same kick stops reaching the receiver.
      • What changing the pitch really costs. Layout-driven skills simply vanish: no fragile-wall snipes and no walls shot down at all on the 3v3 layout or two of the three generated ones, because fragile walls only exist where a wall can be built over a bush. The bots never notice the difference.
      • 3v3 is not 2v2 with an extra bot. It is a separate matchmade format (server.js FORMATS['3v3']) with teamSize: 3 and its own arena, because the main pitch's dense centre does not survive six players. The coordinator still assigns exactly one ball-chaser per side, so the third bot is a second support — watch what MIN_SEP (320 px) does to the shape.

      How current is this page?

      This page is a snapshot, and it says so on purpose. A published artifact is served under a CSP that blocks every external host, so it cannot fetch shared/sim.js from the server at load time — the code it runs is the code that was bundled into it. The stamp below is the exact identity of that bundle, so you can always tell whether what you are watching is current:

      reading build stamp…

      To refresh it: node scripts/build-arena-watch.mjs out.html --from=HEAD and redeploy from the same file path (that keeps the URL). --check out.html answers "has the bundled code changed since?" with an exit code, which is what a hook or a scheduled job can act on. The always-current view is the in-repo twin at /_arena-watch.html on the dev server: it imports /shared live, so it reflects the tree after a restart.

      The button below asks this page's own origin for /shared and compares each module against what was bundled. Served by the game server it tells you exactly which modules have moved on; in the published sandbox it cannot reach anything external — that is the CSP, not a bug — so it says so and hands you the rebuild command. There is no honest way to make a published snapshot pull new code by itself.
